issues.legal_issue: The duration of an implied tenancy created by permitted possession and acceptance of rent is governed by the statutory default where no valid contract fixes a different duration.
material_facts: The occupant remained on the land with the permission of the estate’s representative, who accepted rent from the occupant.
The land was let for the purpose of building structures, not for agriculture or manufacturing.
The parties executed a document purporting to grant a term longer than one year, but the document was inoperative as a lease.
Rent was paid annually for two years, but the court found that the parties did not intend to create a lease for one year at a time.
The dispute arose in an ejectment proceeding, and the validity of the notice to quit was not challenged before the Court.
issues.conclusion: The implied tenancy was from month to month from its inception. The annual rent did not establish a yearly tenancy or a valid contract to the contrary, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act supplies the rule for determining the duration of an implied lease inferred from possession and acceptance of rent, as well as an express lease of uncertain duration. A contract to the contrary may be implied but must be valid; if it is not, section 106 governs. Annual rent may raise a presumption of an annual tenancy, but section 107 requires a registered instrument to create a tenancy from year to year or one reserving yearly rent. The inoperative instrument could not satisfy that requirement, and the parties’ intended term exceeding one year could not properly be replaced by an inferred one-year contract. The Court’s approach is supported by Debendra Nath v. Shyama Prasanna and Sheikh Akloo v. Emaman; Aziz Ahmad v. Alauddin Ahmad, Md. Moosa v. Jaganand, and Matilal v. Darjeeling Municipality were also referred to.

rule.if: is_ejectment_proceeding and permitted_possession and rent_paid_and_accepted and building_purpose and purported_long_term_lease_inoperative and parties_intended_term_exceeding_year

predicates.is_ejectment_proceeding: The dispute is an ejectment proceeding concerning an occupant who claims that the tenancy has ended or has a different duration.
predicates.permitted_possession: The occupant remained on the land with the permission of the person managing or representing the owner’s interests.
predicates.rent_paid_and_accepted: The occupant paid rent and the owner or the owner’s representative accepted it.
predicates.building_purpose: The land was let for the purpose of building structures rather than for agriculture or manufacturing.
predicates.purported_long_term_lease_inoperative: The parties executed a document purporting to grant a term longer than one year, but that document did not operate as a valid lease.
predicates.parties_intended_term_exceeding_year: The circumstances showed that the parties intended a term exceeding one year rather than a sequence of separate one-year tenancies.

issues.definition: When permitted possession and accepted rent occur in an ejectment proceeding involving land let for building, and the purported longer-term lease is inoperative despite the parties’ intent to agree on a term exceeding one year, the tenancy is treated as month to month.
